title: Late-Night Foodie — Awareness → Newsletter Subscription
subtitle: How the post-midnight, food-culture 20-something goes from a first-bite clip to opting in for location drops and insider seasonal access.

doing.text: Scrolling TikTok and Instagram after a late shift, they catch a close-up midnight brisket first-bite clip — or a coworker leaving the bar says "the brisket one" and shows them a photo. Discovery is social and word-of-mouth, inside the service-industry and night-scene crowd.

thinking.text: "Wait — actual smoked brisket at a taco truck, at 1 a.m.? That's not the usual sad late-night option."

channels.text: TikTok, Instagram, word of mouth (service crew / night scene), festival stalls

pains.text: The national feed lands the hook, but the local truck account that would make it feel real and findable nearby is often dormant — so the brand shows up as a vibe, not yet a place they can actually get to tonight.

opps.text: Arm the scene as the discovery engine it already is: feed the food-culture crowd close-up brisket and first-bite clips built for reshare, so social reach compounds into trial rather than evaporating.

doing.text: Watches a few more clips, then tries to pin down where a truck actually is tonight — checks the app and the local Instagram, and pings the group chat: "where do we go?"

thinking.text: "Is this genuinely good or just a good photo — and more urgently, where is it right now, because I'm not chasing a truck across the city at 2 a.m."

channels.text: App, Instagram (local truck account), group chat, TikTok

pains.text: The one question — is this specific truck open now, and exactly where — is the hardest to answer, and late-night makes it worse: the app menu is static and out of sync with the truck board, so intent goes unconverted.

opps.text: Win the real-time certainty battle for the late crowd: a reliable "open now, parked here" answer turns high late-night intent into a first visit — the highest-return move available.

doing.text: Finds the truck after a shift or a show, rolls up with the crew, orders the smoked brisket, and films the unwrap and first bite — steam off the taco, truck lights behind it.

thinking.text: "Okay — this is the real thing. Somebody actually smoked this. That was worth finding."

channels.text: The truck window, TikTok / Instagram story

pains.text: They only got here by guesswork and DMs — and the hero can sell out, with no approved on-brand line when the brisket is gone, risking a first impression of "drove there for nothing."

opps.text: The first midnight bite is the conversion moment — make it effortless to capture and share, and protect hero availability for the late-night occasion so the first visit lands every time.

doing.text: The post-shift / post-show brisket run becomes a standing thing with the crew — a repeatable social ritual the truck is well-positioned to own.

thinking.text: "This is our spot after close — when I can actually find it."

channels.text: The truck, Instagram DMs, group chat, local truck account

pains.text: The ritual is fragile: the truck moves, the local account goes quiet for days, and a drove-there-and-no-truck night breaks the habit — the discovery-to-loyalty chain leaks exactly where it should compound.

opps.text: Own the post-midnight occasion outright: make the truck reliably findable late so the ritual compounds visit over visit into durable habit.

doing.text: Posts the midnight brisket shot, tags the truck, and brings coworkers and the scene along — running genuine word-of-mouth for the brand, quietly and constantly.

thinking.text: "I'm basically doing their marketing for free — out of real affection. The least they can do is be there on the other end."

channels.text: TikTok, Instagram stories, group chat, the local scene

pains.text: The brand often isn't present on the other end — a dormant local account, and in Montreal an English-only presence that reads as a small but real exclusion — which blunts the free amplification a superfan is already generating.

opps.text: Arm the superfan: reshare their content, stay present locally, and show up in genuine fr-CA for Montreal so the scene's word-of-mouth pays off and sets BorderBlend apart in a market most brands under-serve.

doing.text: Opts in enthusiastically — but for one thing above all: a live late-night location drop telling them where the truck is parked tonight, plus insider early access to seasonal previews like Fuego Nights, and joins loyalty when it is genuinely simple.

thinking.text: "If you just tell me where you're parked tonight — and let me in early on the seasonal stuff before it drops — I'm in, in a heartbeat."

channels.text: SMS / push location drops, email newsletter, app loyalty, Instagram

pains.text: Today's loyalty programme is opaque enough that most don't know it exists or abandon the account interface — and generic "ORDER NOW" push, or English-only copy in Montreal, gets them to bail instantly.

opps.text: Convert devotion the brand has already earned into subscription: a "we're parked here tonight" late-night alert, Fuego Nights / seasonal early access, a genuine insider-creator feel, and real Québécois French for Montreal — tie opt-in to a concrete value moment, not brand-story noise.
